newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean officer killed by friendly fire.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean officer killed by friendly fire.

text.p: A South Korean corporal shot dead one of his officers after mistaking him for a North Korean infiltrator during a manhunt for agents who landed by submarine last month, the defence ministry said on Friday.
The 26-year-old captain was shot in the head on Thursday night after the corporal, waiting in an ambush, heard noises and thought it was a North Korean infiltrator, a ministry spokesman said.

He was the fifth South Korean soldier killed in the hunt for the communist agents after their submarine was found grounded on rocks on September 18. Three have died from friendly fire and two were shot and killed by intruders.

"Both soldiers were hunting for the fugitive North Korean infiltrators when the accident occurred," the spokesman said. "The soldier thought the other soldier was a North Korean infiltrator when he heard the sounds in the woods."

South Korean soldiers have killed 11 intruders, found the bodies of another 11 and captured one alive. Thousands of troops are hunting for three more believed to be on the run in mountains on the east coast of the country.

The defence ministry has said it believed the remaining agents killed three South Korean villagers whose bodies were found on Wednesday in the Mount Odae area, about 70 km (44 miles) from where the agents came ashore.
A 67-year-old woman had been bludgeoned before being suffocated, while two men, aged 54 and 45, had been shot. All three had last been seen picking wild mushrooms in the rural area on Tuesday.
Southern troops previously shot dead a civilian by mistake during the search.
U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord met South Korean leaders on Friday to discuss the crisis on the peninsula, which has been divided since the 1950-53 Korean War ended with a ceasefire.
The domestic Yonhap news agency said Lord and South Korean foreign minister Gong Ro-myung met and agreed to strengthen defences against North Korea.
They also discussed Pyongyang's threats of "merciless retaliation" over the deaths of its agents.

The United States maintains 37,000 troops in South Korea. Politicians in South Korea have faulted Washington's restrained response to the submarine incursion, and Lord's mission is aimed at limiting the damage.
